## Plot the remarkable points in the noisy signal

**Objective:** To investigate how adding white noise affects the detection of zero crossings, local maxima, and minima.

### a) Identify remarkable points manually

Before using the detection functions from Section 2, we first examine the noisy signal to identify its remarkable points visually.

We first examine the noisy signal to identify local maxima, minima, and zero crossings by hand before using the detection functions. We use `%matplotlib widget` to zoom in on the signal and inspect individual points more closely.

A remarkable point is identified as follows:

| Point | How to identify it |
|---|---|
| Local maximum | A point higher than its neighboring points |
| Local minimum | A point lower than its neighboring points |
| Positive zero crossing | Signal changes from negative to positive |
| Negative zero crossing | Signal changes from positive to negative |

```{python}
# Enable interactive plotting
%matplotlib widget

# Plot the noisy signal using the existing function
plt.figure(figsize=(9, 4))
plot_signal(t, s_noisy)

plt.title("Noisy signal")
plt.xlabel("Time (s)")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()
```
